executive_summary: Child B of SD-LEO-ORCH-MICHAEL-ROLE-FORMALIZATION-002 gives Michael his database source of truth and the verbs that write it. One migration creates the eleven michael_* tables of spec section 2 in the 20260830_commitments_table.sql posture (RLS, service-role-only policy, REVOKE ALL from anon, authenticated and PUBLIC, COMMENT ON TABLE, natural-key unique index, one DO $verify$ block with positive and negative privilege asserts per table) and ships chairman-gated with no @approved-by marker; the drift-guard ledger is re-seeded in the same PR. The morning-conversation verbs (gmail-act, todoist-act, rule-encode, closure-add, capture, feedback-append) and autonomy-read land as absolute-path scripts under scripts/michael/ so the seat never writes tables directly; rule-encode refuses any auto_apply flip or supersede of an active rule unless a runner-produced Opus verifier verdict file (producer, run id, content hash) is supplied and its hash re-verifies, and the verdict is stored in provenance. autonomy-read computes the approval streak from ledger dispositions at read time with no stored counter, proposes flips only for label, archive and reschedule, and revokes on reopened_at or moved_back_at first. scripts/michael-rules-load.mjs returns rows; scripts/michael-rules-render.mjs writes docs/michael/generated/RULES.md and CLOSURES.md (gitignored) for the chairman only. scripts/michael/retention.mjs nulls prose older than 30 days from a weekly no-credential GHA venue. Every script is inert (exit 0, empty rows, tables_absent=true) until the chairman applies the migration. Explore evidence db87ff67 and VALIDATION evidence 36747d8e (CONDITIONAL_PASS, seven amendments carried here) ground every mechanism claim.

functional_requirements.title: One chairman-gated migration creating the eleven michael_* tables
functional_requirements.description: Add database/migrations/20260906_michael_tables.sql and 20260906_michael_tables_DOWN.sql. Posture per table follows database/migrations/20260830_commitments_table.sql:40-52 (verified by Explore db87ff67): CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, COMMENT ON TABLE naming the SD and spec section, ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, DROP POLICY IF EXISTS + CREATE POLICY <table>_service_role FOR ALL TO service_role USING (true) WITH CHECK (true), REVOKE ALL ON <table> FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC, GRANT ALL TO service_role, and a natural-key UNIQUE INDEX. One DO $verify$ block in the database/migrations/20260803_drive_reports.sql:303-499 shape asserts, for each table, to_regclass IS NOT NULL, relrowsecurity, the policy row, has_table_privilege(anon|authenticated, table, 'SELECT') = false, and has_table_privilege(service_role, table, 'SELECT') = true. Tables and natural keys (spec section 2): michael_rules (domain, rule_key) with domain CHECK IN (gmail, todoist, calendar, tasks, body, brief, capture, youtube), rule_text, rule_json JSONB NULL, status CHECK IN (active, superseded) default active, supersedes UUID NULL referencing michael_rules(id), provenance JSONB NOT NULL, auto_apply BOOLEAN default false, auto_apply_since TIMESTAMPTZ, auto_apply_verb TEXT NULL CHECK IN (label, archive, reschedule), and NO streak columns; michael_gmail_labels (label_id) with name, class, keep_in_inbox, summarize, last_seen_in_gmail_at; michael_closures (closure_key) with topic, keywords TEXT[], closure_text, expires_at, scope, provenance; michael_feedback_ledger (et_date) with landed, friction, dispositions JSONB default '[]', outcome_vs_jobs, acted; michael_feeder_runs (feeder, et_date, attempt) with venue CHECK IN (task_scheduler, gha, seat), status CHECK IN (ok, degraded, failed, skipped, imported), counts JSONB, log_md, started_at, finished_at, model_used, tokens_in, tokens_out; michael_calendar_day (et_date, event_id) with coded_marker, optional, overlap_group; michael_gmail_triage_items (et_date, thread_id) with class, action_intent, action_taken_at, needs_you, needs_you_reason, borderline, rule_key, verified_by, summary, last_message_id, reopened_at; michael_todoist_snapshot (et_date, task_id) with effort_grade, est_minutes, role_tag, proposed_date, proposed_action, chosen_action, mutations_applied JSONB, moved_back_at; michael_brief_runs (et_date) with data_json JSONB, rendered_html, brief_md, assembled_at, rendered_at, verified BOOLEAN default false, verify_notes, enriched_at, surfaced_at; michael_credentials (identifier) with encrypted_blob TEXT, scopes TEXT[], expires_at, last_refreshed_at, last_error; michael_staged_items (id UUID) with kind, payload JSONB, staged_at default now(), dispositioned_at, disposition. Every table carries id UUID PK default gen_random_uuid(), created_at and updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ default now(), and every et_date is DATE. The consumer columns already read by scripts/michael-quiet-tick.mjs:103-113 (michael_gmail_triage_items.et_date/class, michael_todoist_snapshot.et_date/effort_grade, michael_brief_runs.et_date/verified/enriched_at, michael_feeder_runs.et_date/status, michael_staged_items.kind/dispositioned_at) are pinned by the shape test. AMENDED (VALIDATION 36747d8e): the header carries the line '-- @chairman-gated: applied by the chairman after sign-off (Tier 3)' and NO @approved-by marker (the chairman adds it at apply, as PR #8294 did for child A); the DOWN drops the eleven tables in dependency order and nothing else; the migration-dispositions ledger is re-seeded in the same PR with npm run migration:dispositions:seed -- --gaps=<verifier --json> --write so RULE A (scripts/seed-migration-dispositions.mjs:116-138) records the DEFERRED entry and the guard's sync step stays green. AMENDED (VALIDATION): B ships ALL eleven DDL including michael_credentials and michael_brief_runs; children C and E ship code only, never a second migration.

functional_requirements.title: rule-encode with the Opus verifier gate, closure-add, capture, feedback-append
functional_requirements.description: Add scripts/michael/rule-encode.mjs --domain <d> --key <k> --text "..." [--json '...'] --source <channel:ref> [--auto-apply --verb label|archive|reschedule] [--verifier-verdict <path>] [--dry-run]. It writes michael_rules with provenance {ratification_id (nullable), source (channel:ref shape, at least five characters, validated like lib/chairman/ratification-writer.mjs:259-262), uttered_at, encoded_by, verifier} and, when an active row with the same (domain, rule_key) exists, inserts the new row with supersedes = prior.id and updates the prior to status superseded in the same call, naming the replacement exactly as lib/chairman/decision-retirement.mjs:214-227 requires. GATE: whenever the write would set auto_apply true, change auto_apply_verb, or supersede an active rule, the script REFUSES (exit 2, nothing written, refusal names the missing verdict) unless --verifier-verdict points to a runner-produced JSON file {producer: 'opus-verifier', run_id, model (must start with claude-opus), verdict ('approve'|'reject'), reasoning, subject_hash, produced_at}; the script recomputes subject_hash = sha256 of the canonical JSON of {domain, rule_key, rule_text, rule_json, auto_apply, auto_apply_verb, supersedes} and refuses on mismatch, on a non-opus model, on a reject verdict, or on a file older than 24 hours; the accepted verdict is stored verbatim in provenance.verifier. WHY A FILE: the Opus verifier is the seat's own sub-agent (Agent tool) per spec section 3, Max-plan models are reachable only from a Claude Code session, and spec section 0 forbids any API-key billing. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE (VALIDATION 36747d8e amendment 2): scripts/execute-team.mjs:151-168 and lib/drain-orchestrator.mjs:297 do spawn a headless claude --print session without an API key, but that path requires --dangerously-skip-permissions (declined by the chairman for worker seats on 2026-09-05), adds a detached session's quota and latency inside a synchronous morning verb, and would make rule-encode author the evidence it gates (ratification 6c263823) — so the verdict is produced outside the writer and hash-bound, in the lib/chairman/ratification-writer.mjs:293-295 quote_hash shape. After a successful write the script regenerates RULES.md via scripts/michael-rules-render.mjs. Add scripts/michael/closure-add.mjs --key --topic --text [--keywords a,b] [--expires <iso>] [--scope] --source, scripts/michael/capture.mjs --text [--kind capture] staging a michael_staged_items row, and scripts/michael/feedback-append.mjs --date <et_date, default today via etDateStr> [--landed] [--friction] [--outcome] [--acted] --disposition '{topic, rule_key, proposed, chosen, reasoning}' upserting the ledger row by et_date and appending the disposition, with chosen CHECKed in the script to approve|override|auto|skip.

functional_requirements.title: autonomy-read: read-time streaks, reversible-verb proposals, outcome-first revocation
functional_requirements.description: Add scripts/michael/autonomy-read.mjs [--json] [--rule <key>] [--threshold <n>]. For each active michael_rules row it walks michael_feedback_ledger.dispositions in et_date order and computes the trailing consecutive count of chosen='approve' on dispositions whose rule_key matches (an override, skip or auto entry for that rule resets the streak; days without an entry for that rule are ignored). Threshold: --threshold, else the active michael_rules row domain=brief rule_key=autonomy_threshold rule_json.value, else 7. A proposal {rule_key, streak, verb, action:'flip_auto_apply'} is emitted only when streak >= threshold, auto_apply is false, and the proposed verb is label, archive or reschedule; complete and delete never propose. Revocations are emitted first: {rule_key, action:'revoke', signal:'reopened_at'} when any michael_gmail_triage_items row with rule_key = that rule and action_intent archive has reopened_at IS NOT NULL after action_taken_at, {signal:'moved_back_at'} when any michael_todoist_snapshot row whose proposed_action names that rule has moved_back_at set, and {signal:'three_overrides'} when the last three dispositions for that rule are consecutive overrides. Output {tables_absent, threshold, proposals[], revocations[], streaks{}}; with tables absent it prints empty arrays and exits 0. No counter is ever stored (spec section 7, Solomon Q4). The script only reads; applying a flip is rule-encode's job through the FR-3 gate, and a revoke stages a rule-edit proposal in michael_staged_items kind=rule_edit when --stage is passed.

functional_requirements.title: gmail-act and todoist-act
functional_requirements.description: Add scripts/michael/gmail-act.mjs --thread <id> --label <id> [--archive|--unarchive] [--date <et_date>]. The API leg resolves lazily: it imports lib/michael/gmail-client.mjs (child C's deliverable, built on the spec section 4 module lib/integrations/google/chairman-oauth.js; its contract is modifyThread({threadId, addLabelIds, removeLabelIds}) returning {ok, modified}) inside try/catch and, when the module is absent, exits 2 with the refusal GMAIL_CLIENT_ABSENT naming child C — nothing is written. When present it calls the client, then upserts michael_gmail_triage_items (et_date, thread_id) setting action_intent, action_taken_at = now() and, on --unarchive, reopened_at = now() (the revoke signal FR-4 reads). Explore db87ff67 confirmed no Gmail API client exists in the repo. Add scripts/michael/todoist-act.mjs reschedule --task <id> --date <YYYY-MM-DD> | complete --task <id> | add --content "..." [--project] [--due] | comment --task <id> --text "...", built on lib/integrations/todoist/todoist-sync.js createTodoistClient() (TODOIST_API_TOKEN, a service token, not an Anthropic API key) using the @doist/todoist-api-typescript updateTask/closeTask/addTask/addComment methods; every verb upserts michael_todoist_snapshot (et_date, task_id) appending the mutation to mutations_applied and setting chosen_action, and a reschedule whose new date differs from the row's proposed_date stamps moved_back_at = now(). Both scripts accept --dry-run (print the intended API call and row, write nothing) and --json.

functional_requirements.title: retention.mjs and its weekly no-credential workflow
functional_requirements.description: Add scripts/michael/retention.mjs in the scripts/retention-enforce.js:183-240 shape: dry-run by default printing per-table candidate counts, --apply executing, --days <n> default 30, fail-soft per table, exit 0 with tables_absent=true when the migration is unapplied. Apply: UPDATE michael_brief_runs SET rendered_html = NULL, brief_md = NULL WHERE et_date < cutoff AND (rendered_html IS NOT NULL OR brief_md IS NOT NULL); UPDATE michael_gmail_triage_items SET summary = NULL, needs_you_reason = NULL WHERE et_date < cutoff; DELETE FROM michael_calendar_day WHERE et_date < cutoff. Rules, closures, dispositions, counts and every non-prose column are never touched. Every run (dry and apply) inserts a michael_feeder_runs row feeder='retention', et_date = today (etDateStr), attempt = 1 + max(attempt) for that day, venue='gha', status ok|failed, counts = the per-table numbers, so the age of the newest retention row is the liveness signal (no new table). WHY NOT retention-enforce.js: its archive-before-delete would copy personal calendar rows into retention_archive indefinitely, contradicting spec section 2 data handling; prose is nulled in place instead. Add .github/workflows/michael-retention-cron.yml mirroring .github/workflows/retention-enforce-cron.yml:20-60 (weekly cron '0 4 * * 0' + workflow_dispatch, permissions contents: read, concurrency group, env only SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, the apply step, no user credential and no encryption key per ratification 0daf3bd8).

functional_requirements.title: Tests that pin shape and refusal paths without a scratch database
functional_requirements.description: tests/unit/migrations/michael-tables-migration-shape.test.js loops MICHAEL_TABLES (eleven names) asserting for each: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.<t>, a UNIQUE INDEX on the spec natural key, COMMENT ON TABLE, ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE POLICY <t>_service_role, REVOKE ALL ON public.<t> FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC, GRANT ALL ... TO service_role, has_table_privilege ASSERTs for anon and authenticated inside DO $verify$; plus: no streak column names (streak, approve_count, consecutive), the auto_apply_verb CHECK, the feeder_runs venue CHECK, the consumer columns of FR-1, the '-- @chairman-gated' line present and /^--\s*@approved-by/m absent, the DOWN dropping exactly eleven tables and no column. Script tests (vitest, injected clients built as in scripts/michael-quiet-tick.test.js): rule-encode refuses flip/supersede without a verdict, with a non-opus model, with a hash mismatch, with a reject verdict, and with a stale file; accepts an opus approve verdict, stores provenance.verifier, and marks the prior row superseded naming the new id; autonomy-read: six approves then override yields no proposal, seven consecutive approves on a label rule yields one, seven on a complete rule yields none, reopened_at yields an immediate revoke, three consecutive overrides yields a revoke, absent tables yields empty output; feedback-append appends with the chosen grain and rejects an unknown chosen; todoist-act stamps moved_back_at only when the reschedule differs from proposed_date; gmail-act exits 2 GMAIL_CLIENT_ABSENT when the seam is missing and stamps reopened_at on --unarchive when present; retention selects only rows older than the cutoff, never touches rules or closures, and writes the feeder_runs stamp on dry runs too.

technical_requirements.title: Inert until applied
technical_requirements.description: Every script wraps its michael_* reads and writes through lib/michael/db.mjs so a missing relation (42P01, PGRST205, COUNT_UNMEASURABLE) yields tables_absent=true, empty rows and exit 0 for reads, and a named refusal exit 2 for writes; no script throws on an unapplied migration.

technical_requirements.title: Absolute-path verbs, no direct table writes by the seat
technical_requirements.description: Verbs live under scripts/michael/ and are invoked as node scripts/michael/<verb>.mjs from the repo root (chairman ruling B, QF-646 lineage); CLAUDE_MICHAEL.md already forbids the seat writing tables directly, so every write path is a script with --dry-run and --json.

technical_requirements.title: Provenance and hash binding
technical_requirements.description: michael_rules.provenance is JSONB {ratification_id, source, uttered_at, encoded_by, verifier}; verifier is the verbatim verdict file whose subject_hash rule-encode recomputed (sha256 over canonical JSON with sorted keys). The extension of the spec section 2 provenance list by encoded_by and verifier is recorded here so the shape test asserts the superset.

technical_requirements.title: Supersession names its replacement
technical_requirements.description: A superseded rule row always has a successor: the new row carries supersedes = prior.id and the prior is flipped to status superseded in the same script call; a prior with status superseded is never re-superseded (decision-retirement.mjs:214-227 precedent).

technical_requirements.title: Personal-data posture
technical_requirements.description: Bodies are never stored (only summary for summarize classes); RLS plus REVOKE makes every michael_* table unreadable to anon and authenticated; the spec states plainly that service-role holders can read them; prose is nulled at 30 days; GET /api/michael/* is child C/E behind requireAuth at server/index.js:248-281 and is untouched here.

technical_requirements.title: Lint and guard compliance
technical_requirements.description: The migration passes secdef-execute-revoke-lint (no SECURITY DEFINER functions are created, REVOKE names PUBLIC and anon/authenticated), alter-default-override-lint (no ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT), rls-anon-tenant-predicate-lint, eol-renormalization-lint, control-seed-test-lint (no new control), count-truncation-diff-lint (bounded selects carry count: 'exact'), and the session-coordination classguard (no session_coordination inserts).

technical_requirements.description: PR 1 migration + DOWN + shape test + ledger re-seed; PR 2 lib/michael/db.mjs, rules-load, rules-render, .gitignore; PR 3 rule-encode, closure-add, capture, feedback-append + tests; PR 4 autonomy-read + tests; PR 5 gmail-act, todoist-act + tests; PR 6 retention + workflow + tests. Each PR carries its justification when over 100 LOC.
